title: Fast Estimation for Forest Matrix of Signed Graphs
claim: A small example structure admits a finite, enumerable set of valid substructures, which grounds the abstract theorem in a concrete case.
layout: Left input graph, right 2x6 grid of enumerated forests, highlighted cells
description: The figure has a wide strip split into two parts. On the left is a large square panel showing a toy signed directed graph called G0. It has three nodes (1, 2, 3) arranged in a triangle. Edges are labeled +1 or −1, and one pair of nodes is joined by bidirectional arcs. To the right is a 2×6 grid of small panels labeled φ1 to φ12. Each panel shows the same three nodes with a different generalized spanning converging forest. Roots are filled in blue, and the other nodes are white with arrows pointing toward the roots. The last three panels, φ10 to φ12, have a yellow background. These are the forests that contain cycles, and they have no blue roots. The eye goes first to the yellow cells and the graph on the left.
caption: A toy signed graph $\calG_0$ with its $12$ generalized spanning converging forests. Blue nodes are roots.
abstract: The forest matrix of a signed graph plays an important role in network science and social opinion dynamics, yet existing algorithms are mainly designed for unsigned graphs and are difficult to extend to signed graphs. In this paper, we study the problem of efficiently estimating the forest matrix of signed graphs with n nodes and introduce the signed forest matrix theorem, which establishes the relationship between generalized spanning converging forests and the forest matrix. Based on this result, we propose a novel algorithm GSCF, built on a variant of loop-erased random walks, to generate generalized spanning converging forests in expected O(n) time. We further develop two sampling algorithms, FMDE and FMDE+, for estimating the diagonal of the forest matrix, both with time complexity O(ln), where l is the number of samples. Extensive experiments on various signed graphs show that our methods achieve high estimation accuracy, significantly improve computational efficiency, and scale to graphs with over twenty million nodes. Our source code is publicly available on https://github.com/HaoxinSun98/SignedForestDiagonal.
